hypothesis: The champion sets THP enabled=always but leaves defrag=madvise, so when no huge page is free the kernel serves a 4K page instead of compacting. THP was worth -2.7% here, which means the heap does benefit from 2 MiB pages; defrag=always makes the allocation actually happen under fragmentation, at the cost of allocation-time stalls. Tests whether the THP win is currently being left on the table.
llm_commentary: THP defrag=always on top of the champion is neutral: 4.34s vs 4.31s, i.e. marginally worse and inside run spread. So the -2.7% THP win is already being collected with the AL2023 default defrag=madvise — the boxes are freshly booted and barely fragmented, so huge-page allocations succeed without compaction, and forcing compaction only adds allocation-time stalls. Useful as a bound: the THP gain comes from 2 MiB pages being used, not from how hard the kernel tries to find them. A long-lived, fragmented node might see the opposite, which is worth re-testing on a box that has been running for days rather than minutes. Champion unchanged at 4.31s (PGO + THP enabled=always, defrag left at the default).
